newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-GRAND SLAM CUP -- THE MEN CHASING THE MONEY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAND SLAM CUP -- THE MEN CHASING THE MONEY.

text.p: The Grand Slam Cup, which starts on Tuesday, is the richest tournament in tennis with $6 million prize money. Here are some facts and figures about the event:
Established 1990 in Munich. Played on indoor carpet court in Munich's Olympic arena which was built for the 1972 Summer Games.
Participants - The best performers from the four grand slams of the year (Wimbledon and the French, U.S. and Australian Opens) qualify to take part in the 16-man knockout tournament.
Previous winners: 1990-Pete Sampras (U.S.), 1991-David Wheaton (U.S.), 1992-Michael Stich (Germany), 1993-Petr Korda (Czech Republic), 1994-Magnus Larsson (Sweden), 1995-Goran Ivanisevic (Croatia).
In addition the winners of Wimbledon and three Opens are awarded $250,000 for playing in the Cup. If a player has won more than one grand slam he is awarded $250,000 for each victory.
Grand Slam champions participating in 1996: Becker (Australian Open), Yevgeny Kafelnikov (French Open), Richard Krajicek (Wimbledon)

Tuesday (starting at 1200 GMT) - Stich v Tim Henman (Britain), Boris Becker (Germany) v Jason Stoltenberg (Australia), MaliVai Washington (U.S) v Krajicek (Netherlands), Marc Rosset (Switzerland) v Jim Courier (U.S.)

Wednesday (starting at 1200 GMT): Ivanisevic v Mikael Tillstrom (Sweden), Andre Agassi (U.S.) v Mark Woodforde (Australia), Jakob Hlasek (Switzerland) v Cedric Pioline (France), Kafelnikov (Russia) v Thomas Enqvist (Sweden)
